$description: E3 Center design tokens — the single source of truth. Platform-neutral (W3C Design Tokens format) so one file can emit web CSS, a slide theme and print swatches. Nothing consumes this by hand: run build_tokens.py. Every colour is either taken from the logo or derived from one that is, and every text colour is verified against BOTH surfaces (paper and the tint band) by validate_tokens.py.

contrastTargetText.$description: Derived text colours must clear this on every surface. Above AA's 4.5 for headroom.

surfaces.$description: Text must pass against every surface listed here.

mark.$description: The seven colours in e3-center-logo-inline.svg, verbatim. The specification everything else derives from. Never consumed directly by a component.

wordmarkNavy.$description: The navy 'E3 Center' is set in.

paper.$description: Page background. Warmth +3 (R−B), chosen from a seven-step ramp. Also the slide background and the print stock reference.

surface.$description: Section band. mark.paleRibbon at 30% over paper.

line.$description: Hairlines and dividers. mark.greyBlue at 55% over paper — the mark's own neutral, so rules stay neutral rather than olive.

ink.$description: All primary text. mark.wordmarkNavy unchanged, so body copy and the lockup are the same colour. 7.64:1 on paper, 6.86:1 on surface.

muted.$description: Secondary text. Ink lightened to the limit that still clears the target on BOTH surfaces. 5.80:1 / 5.21:1.

structure.$description: Rules, chart axes, header. mark.deep unchanged. 7.22:1 / 6.48:1.

graphic.$description: mark.teal exactly. Fills, marks, non-text. 4.36:1 on surface — NOT for text.

text.$description: Links, active states, and anywhere the accent must be read rather than seen. Derived from mark.teal and checked against its OWN 12-14% tint as well as paper and the band, because every consumer sits on one: 6.04:1 paper, 5.42:1 band, 5.02:1 on the darkest tint in use. Replaces --accent-ink, which mixed teal 30% toward navy and landed at hue 195 - six degrees off plain --ink, so it barely read as an accent at all. This keeps mark.teal's exact 176.

marker.$description: mark.moss. The field marker: underline bars, the 3E dot, directional glyphs, the energy dashes in the hero. A distinct UI role from field.energy — the same hue doing structural work rather than coding a research area. Never text (2.18:1).

color.$fieldNote: Field coding (the three E's) deliberately does NOT live here. It stays on the existing vivid trio — yellow / orange / green in general.css — because the mark's seven colours sit within ~40 degrees of each other and moss/sage/grey-blue are far harder to tell apart as field codes than yellow/orange/green. Same conclusion as the category badges: the mark supplies identity, not distinguishability.

badge.$description: Category and status badges. Each entry is an anchor hue plus a text colour derived to clear the contrast target on THREE backdrops: its own badge tint, paper, and the section band. The old system checked only the tint and paper — and against a stale hardcoded paper at that — so a badge sitting in a tinted section was never verified at all.

tint.$description: Badge background is the anchor at this fraction over paper.

category.$description: Five hues that must be told apart at badge size. Only two come from the mark — the mark's seven colours sit in a narrow green-blue band, and five badges cut from it would be indistinguishable. The rest are a declared extension held to the same derivation discipline, not an ad-hoc palette.

faculty.$description: .news-row-badge tints --marker directly at 22%, so faculty has no anchor token of its own — only the text tier is named. emitAnchor false keeps --cat-faculty from being emitted dead.

status.$description: Three states. ok and progress reuse the student and faculty hues deliberately — a green 'published' and a green 'student' never appear in the same control, and adding hues costs distinguishability elsewhere.

weight.$description: Size carries hierarchy; weight only whispers. Outfit is geometric, and heavy weights in a geometric sans read cartoonish — which is the register we are moving away from.

heading.$description: Small UI only: eyebrows, badges, buttons

scale.$description: Explicit px per tier. The old system scaled the root 12.5% down on phone and then had to bump the LABEL group back UP to clear the WCAG floor — a correction for a problem it created. Defining each tier outright removes both. Tiers: phone ≤600, tablet 601–1024, laptop 1025–1439, wide ≥1440.

h1.$description: Page titles on subpages. Added 2026-08-12 after reference research: GOV.UK 48, USWDS 40-48, Stripe 40, MIT/Princeton ~30. Sits a major-third step above h2, well below the hero-only display tier.

eyebrow.$description: Flat at 12px. 11px falls under the legibility floor at 375, and a phone-only bump would reintroduce the very exception the explicit scale exists to remove — 12 vs 11 is imperceptible at desktop anyway.

zhBonus.$description: Added to the Latin value — CJK needs more leading at equal size.

statement.$description: Slogan-scale type — fewer characters per line at display size.

space.$description: Quarter-rem ladder: the step number is the value in 0.25rem units, so --space-4 is 1rem. This is the scale the site already uses, recorded here rather than replaced — an earlier draft invented a geometric scale whose 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10 collided with these, which would have silently changed --space-8 from 32px to 64px everywhere it is used.

radius.$description: One radius, and zero for full-bleed. Flattening is the change that worked; pills and large radii are what we moved away from.

motion.$description: All of it sits behind prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

ambient.$description: Minimum for looping artwork. Motion shows the subject's world operating; it never performs for attention.

breakpoint.$description: Four tiers. Test at 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440 / 1920; 375 and 1024 sit on boundaries deliberately, because that is where off-by-one media-query bugs surface.
